cells.tense: You are here at the table with the pen, and what counts shows up before you can argue for it.
cells.act: set one rule that makes the rest easier
cells.ask: Take something your people already carry — a soup at the turn of the season, how the room goes quiet at certain news. Set a single rule for passing it on: who keeps it, when it gets done, what makes it count. Then leave the week alone and watch.
cells.core:
In a shared room, what counts as worth keeping tends to arrive before the reasons do. A version of the story gets told and one part of it sounds like the true part. A practice comes up again and you can feel whether it still has a body on it. Moving while not yet sure is rarer than it sounds, and it is what others are borrowing when they lean on your read.

Give that read a form it can outlast you. Take one piece of what your people carry and put a small structure under it: who keeps it, when it gets said or done, what makes it count as carried. It doesn't need defending. It needs a wall around it. Then step back and watch whether the week holds the thing up without your hand on it.
cells.sheetLine: Set one wall around what your people already keep.
cells.verb: seeing what matters before the reasons arrive
cells.place: where a group keeps what it has found worth carrying

cells.tense: You will have read the whole shelf before you speak, bracing for a future where you are finally ready.
cells.act: move toward the thing you actually want
cells.ask: A shared thing — a festival, a recipe, a story your people tell — the loss of which would sting most. Go and stand inside it before you have studied it. Stay for what happens. Let it matter to you where the people it matters to can see.
cells.core:
You are bracing for a day when the whole picture will finally be in hand and it will be safe to open your mouth. So you collect versions, compare sources, keep the tab open, and the occasions themselves slide past while the file grows. The picture has stopped being a window and become a wall, and the shelf got heavy.

What still pulls at you is not the entry; it is the thing the entry is about. Let yourself want that thing plainly, just to yourself. Then walk toward it — one shared occasion, standing in the middle of it, taking part before you have earned the right to explain it. A glow comes off what is genuinely lived, and you can turn toward a light long before you can describe it.

cells.tense: You stood at that door some time back, and here you are still asking whether it was real.
cells.act: move through the fog without demanding the map
cells.ask: Next time a shared room puzzles you — a table you can't read, a mood you can't name — stay in it a while without deciding what it means. Hand no one your reading of it, and do the plain next thing that's in front of you.
cells.core:
A room you know how to read, and you have been going around asking other people to confirm what you picked up before you will move on it. Impressions land and you go back over them looking for a warrant that isn't coming. The ear is fine. It has been waiting at the spot where you stopped walking.

One step needs one step's light. Pick a shared thing you move through by feel — a table, a wake, a song that belongs to a particular week — and do the next small thing with it without going to anyone first. What you can see comes back by being used, not by being confirmed. Fog doesn't need to clear for the foot to land.

cells.tense: You are setting the order of things in this shared room, and you believe the hand on the page is someone else's.
cells.act: adjust the share until it is fair, then stop
cells.ask: Somewhere in this last stretch you took on more than your half or let someone carry part of yours. Fix that one imbalance, once, and when it's square, walk away. No explaining, no thanks needed, no going back over it after.
cells.core:
Choices in this shared room keep coming out right and you keep calling it luck. The table settled that way by itself. You happened to bring the right book. Someone in you has been weighing what to keep and what to let go, and it has gone well, and no one has signed the page.

You can see it plainly in what you have swapped with people: what moved one way and what moved back. Go find one. A sentence you gave, a silence you were generous with, a load you took off someone so they could rest. Set the other half beside it. See both halves once, then let the account close. A person who notices what passed between two people is already fair to both.

attempts.check: The record does not support the claim that others have stopped asking what you think or that a particular person holds a memory the teller wants back; it says only that perception lands without argument, so the reader may say 'I'm not confused, I just haven't decided.' The asks survive being wrong: they are small acts of noticing, structure, direction, and fair exchange that work even if the read misses. The sentence that serves the writer is 'you already know this' — it tells the person what they want to hear instead of describing what is happening.

attempts.check: The record supports only that perception lands without argument and that the person trusts what they notice more than they trust the trail of reasons; it does not support claims that others rely on their reading, that they once knew and lost it, or that anyone is waiting on them. A reader could say 'I'm not stuck, I've just been busy' or 'I'm not confused about what matters, I just don't like the options' — the cells must leave room for that. The asks survive a wrong read: each is a small act of holding, wanting, stepping, or exchanging that teaches something even if it misses. The sentence that serves the writer is 'you knew this before anyone told you' — it flatters without describing. Cut all person-certifications and the word 'knowing' as a noun.
